fresh_topic_ideas: A 45‑year‑old woman presents with progressive jaundice; labs show isolated alkaline phosphatase elevation; MRI reveals cholangiocarcinoma; initially misdiagnosed as gallstones.

A 19‑year‑old man arrives with sudden severe chest pain; troponin is normal but ECG shows diffuse ST elevation; coronary angiography is clean; later diagnosed with myopericarditis linked to a novel antiviral.
A 62‑year‑old patient reports unexplained weight loss; labs reveal hypercalcemia with low PTH; PET scan shows a solitary lung nodule; biopsy uncovers ectopic production of 1,25‑dihydroxyvitamin D.

A 34‑year‑old woman experiences recurrent seizures; serum ammonia is markedly elevated despite normal liver function; MRI shows bilateral basal ganglia hyperintensity; discovered urea cycle disorder uncovering the first arginine analog treatment.

A 58‑year‑old man reports chronic cough and night sweats; chest X‑ray is normal; bronchoalveolar lavage reveals atypical lymphocytes; later identified as hypersensitivity pneumonitis triggered by a novel industrial solvent.

A 41‑year-old woman presents with severe hyponatremia; serum osmolality is low; MRI brain shows empty sella; initially treated for SIADH, later found to have adrenal insufficiency due to autoimmune polyglandular syndrome.

A 50‑year-old woman presents with persistent migraine‑like headaches; CT scan is negative; CSF analysis shows elevated protein; nerve conduction studies reveal demyelinating neuropathy; diagnosed with neurosarcoidosis, prompting the first use of a TNF‑alpha inhibitor.

A 29‑year-old female presents with unexplained bruising; platelet count is normal but bleeding time is prolonged; bone marrow biopsy reveals megakaryocyte dysfunction; later identified as a congenital Bernard‑Soulier syndrome, guiding development of a synthetic platelet mimetic.

A 66‑year-old patient reports progressive muscle weakness; CK levels are mildly elevated; EMG shows myopathic changes; muscle biopsy reveals inclusion bodies; initially misdiagnosed as polymyositis, later recognized as sporadic inclusion‑body myositis guiding the first anti‑amyloid therapy.

A 55‑year-old man experiences sudden onset of tinnitus and vertigo; audiometry is normal; MRI shows subtle cerebellar infarct; later linked to a rare thrombosis of the internal auditory artery caused by a novel oral anticoagulant.

A 48‑year-old woman presents with refractory hypertension; plasma renin activity is suppressed; adrenal CT shows a 2 cm mass; biochemical workup uncovers cortisol‑producing adrenal adenoma, leading to the first use of a selective glucocorticoid receptor antagonist.

A 70‑year-old patient reports sudden onset of bilateral leg weakness; MRI spine shows longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis; CSF reveals oligoclonal bands; initially treated for multiple sclerosis, later identified as paraneoplastic syndrome related to a hidden ovarian carcinoma.
